reader.notes: Each RD gets its own engine over the one connector the FD registers, bound by the FD's REPORT clause regardless of order; no edition switch on this path.

refuter.evidence: multi_code-001 (--std 85): FD PRT REPORTS ARE R-A R-B, R-A CODE "A1" paged (PAGE LIMIT 4), R-B CODE "B2" unpaged, GENERATEs interleaved, R-B TERMINATEd and re-INITIATEd while R-A continues: every line of both reports reaches the one file in execution order with its own code (A1HD-A, A1AAA 1, B2BBB 1, ... B2BBB 7, A1AAA 7), R-A's page advance written as a form feed on the shared stream. The rule only says the file contains more than one report, which holds. cite.py: 'OK  §1985:XIII.3.3.4 GR1  (3.3.4 General Rules)  the text is in GR1'. The uncoded blank lines of 1985-GR-XIII.3.2.4-2 would make such a file inseparable by code when a report skips lines; that is recorded there.
